reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.SimplePredictable.N -- reading (locked before any Lean)

Paper notion: none directly (see the class SimplePredictable): in a simple predictable process
phi = sum_{i<N} xi_i 1_{(t_i,t_{i+1}]}, N is the number of partition intervals (equivalently the
partition has N+1 points t_0..t_N). A faithful Lean field is a natural number indexing the
intervals/points consistently with the fields partition and xi (xi indexed by i < N, partition by
i <= N, or an equivalent off-by-one convention used consistently). Edge cases: N = 0 (no
intervals, phi = 0) is a legitimate element (the zero simple process). Any consistent indexing
convention is harmless; it only matters that eval and simpleIntegral sum over exactly the
intervals the structure describes.

Paper context (sec. 2, sec. 3, sec. 4, App. A). Standing basis: (Omega,F,(F_t),P) satisfying the usual
conditions, horizon T>0, d-dimensional Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random
measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E,E);
(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial
sigma-field F_0. Stochastic integrals int Z dW (Z in H^2_W: R^{m x d}-valued predictable,
E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 dt < oo) and int int U dNtilde (U in H^2_N) are the L^2 (Ito /
compensated-Poisson isometry) integrals; they are true L^2 martingales, cadlag, and are used in
identities holding a.s. for every t (sec. 3, "solution"). The paper never constructs these
integrals itself: it takes the standard construction (Applebaum sec. 4, He-Wang-Yan). So every
unit below is infrastructure: the paper's notion is the textbook one, and a faithful Lean
definition is one that (together with the other definitions) yields the textbook object on the
paper's basis for every integrand the paper's claims use; junk values outside that class are
harmless only if every proposition restricts to the class.

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.SimplePredictable.N (ItoSimpleIntegrand.lean:32-33)

Reading: N = number of partition intervals, indexing consistent with partition and xi; N = 0 the
zero process. Lean: N : Nat, partition : Fin (N+1) -> R (N+1 points), xi : Fin N -> Omega -> R (one
coefficient per interval), eval and simpleIntegral sum over i : Fin N with interval
(partition i.castSucc, partition i.succ]. Consistent indexing; N = 0 gives the empty sum (zero
process, zero integral). Matches the reading exactly.
Verdict: faithful.
